reforms.description: The federal government announced an additional C$1.3 billion programme for science and technology over five years, representing a significant increase in public R&D funding.
reforms.package_name: Federal Science and Technology Investment Programme (1988)
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Increased public R&D funding expands the research base and human capital, supporting long-term productivity and innovation capacity.
reforms.status_evidence: Text states 'announced an additional C$1.3 billion programme'.
reforms.importance_rationale: Described as a significant increase in public R&D funding with C$1.3 billion over five years, representing a substantial system-wide investment.
reforms.source_quote: The federal government announces an additional C$1.3 billion programme for science and technology over the next five years.

reforms.description: Quebec's budget included incentives to stimulate R&D as part of new policy initiatives, reflecting a provincial commitment to support research and development activities.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: R&D incentives lower the cost of innovation for firms, encouraging private investment in research and development.
reforms.status_evidence: Text indicates Quebec's budget 'included incentives' as part of new policy initiatives, suggesting announcement rather than implementation.
reforms.importance_rationale: Described as part of new policy initiatives without indication of scale or structural significance; appears to be a provincial-level incentive scheme.
reforms.source_quote: Better-than-expected 1986/87 outcome has permitted new initiatives such as low-income relief, incentives to stimulate R&D and increased capital spending.
